text: When the app works, it’s great. It is literally a daily need for me, and has been for years. Lately, and for a few months now, my entries will not save, or will only partially save. I lose WAY TOO MUCH. On top of that, stoic has been running smoothly on my iPhone, but when it comes to my MacBook, it’s useless. I can pretty much only type an empty page journal. I am completely unable to do my daily check in. The Home page doesn’t even show anything. All of these flaws are extremely annoying, and are making the app unusable.

title: Subscription Spam Kills UX
text:
As a first-time user who just wanted to learn more about and explore the app, the first five or ten minutes with it was awful and frustrating.

I just wanted to see the interface and determine whether or not I might like it.  

Instead, I got hit with a bunch of popups, subscription paywalls, rating requests, and more *constantly* within the first five minutes — to the point that this “mental health companion” app was actively fighting me while I was trying to figure it out.

I get that subscriptions are important.  I don’t even mind paying for something I like.  But when I’m spammed so much in the first few minutes that I can’t even figure it out, the ask comes across as greedy and unhelpful.

Once I cleared the constant popups, I tried to click around and gain a better understanding of how the app functions.  Nope:  More popups and paywalls.

Based on other reviews, some users are having better luck.  I still don’t know if this app is for me … but after all the paywall spam, I have no interest in continuing.

Devs, please consider implementing a better onboarding flow for users and asking for money *after* someone has a chance to get their bearings.

title: What happened to the app?
text: I used to go there and read stoic quotes and stories.  Now they all seem to be gone.  Now, if you want to read anything there, it will have to be your journal (which isn’t going to help me) or by reading content from people I’ve never heard of (whom I don’t trust since I don’t know them). No Marcus Aurelius quotes, no Seneca quotes, no quotes from anyone that I could find except from modern day people who think they know stoicism.  I’d rather stick to the people who I know and admire that have been around for centuries.   And every other click shows a page to “buy” the app on a never ending monthly (or annual) plan.  Sounds more commercial now than stoic.

title: Charged before trial ended

Honestly this price is steep as it is, at least follow through with the heads up you promised me.

title: Daily Prompts + Follow Ups
text: I’ve used the free version for a few years now and I loved that it would prompt me to start my day with my three focus areas + questions that tie into those + gratitude questions. Then in the evening, the prompt would be essentially a follow up of those initial questions. Now the daily check-ins are just one simple question with no follow up. What happened?!?!

title: Beautiful app, but frustrating to use
text: Love the idea of this app and I really wanted to like using it based on the onboarding experience. Once I got into my first daily reflection, I found that all of the prompts after the first “How are you feeling today?” were not functional. It seemed like they were stuck loading content from some server somewhere, which confused me since these were supposed to just be pre-configured static questions that I would have expected to be saved on-device. Perhaps a victim of too many new years resolutions. Definitely expected more at this price point, I wound up ending my free trial.

title: Don’t pay for premium
text: I paid for premium and the journal entries do not sync across devices. I reached out to support after a did the troubleshooting suggested on their FAQ. Support wasn’t helpful. A great journaling app, but very disappointing that premium only does half of what it says it does. Support was no help; took forever to get in touch with them, then told me to troubleshoot the syncing which I did before I contacted them.
